# Qi2 vs. Qi2.2 vs. MagSafe

| | **Qi2** | **Qi2.2 (Qi2 25W)** | **MagSafe** |
|---|---|---|---|
| Who makes it | Wireless Power Consortium (WPC), the open standard | WPC, the newer version of Qi2 | Apple's branded system |
| Max speed | 15W | 25W | 15W for most iPhones, up to 25W for newer ones |
| Magnets | Yes, magnetic ring for alignment | Yes | Yes |

**Qi2** is the open standard that added a magnetic ring to Qi wireless charging. The Verge notes it was built with contributions from Apple's MagSafe tech ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)). The magnets line the phone up with the charger, which improves efficiency and speed, and it charges at up to 15W ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)).

**Qi2.2** is the same idea at higher power. The WPC calls it Qi2 25W, and it delivers nearly 70% more power than Qi2. It can take a phone from 0 to 50% in about 30 minutes ([WPC](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/)). Products began getting certified in July 2025 ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/news/708060/qi-2-2-certification-25w-wpc-belkin-anker-ugreen-aukey)).

**MagSafe** is Apple's own branding. Apple certifies MagSafe accessories for 15W on most iPhones and up to 25W on the iPhone 16 and 17 series. Certified MagSafe chargers also include an NFC antenna so the iPhone can identify them, and a magnetometer to prevent compass interference ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). Apple's current MagSafe Charger is also certified for Qi2 25W ([Apple](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m)).

## What matters when buying
- **iPhone speeds vary by model.** Apple says the iPhone 17 series, iPhone 16 Plus, and iPhone 16 Pro Max get up to 25W. The iPhone 16 and 16 Pro get 22.5W, and the iPhone Air gets 20W. The iPhone 15 and earlier, and the 17e, get 15W ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **You need the right power adapter.** For 25W, Apple recommends a 30W or higher USB-C adapter. For 15W, it recommends 20W or higher ([Apple Support](https://support.apple.com/en-ie/105047)).
- **"MagSafe-compatible" is not the same as certified.** Uncertified chargers are usually just 7.5W with a magnet ring, and they take about twice as long to charge in the early stages ([Macworld](https://www.macworld.com/article/668980/best-magsafe-chargers.html)). To check, look for the Qi2 logo or search the [WPC certified product database](https://www.wirelesspowerconsortium.com/standards/qi-wireless-charging/).
- **Android support is limited.** The Pixel 10, 10 Pro, and 10 Pro Fold support Qi2 at 15W, and the 10 Pro XL supports Qi2.2 at 25W. Samsung's Galaxy S26 lineup is "Qi2 Ready," which needs a magnetic case ([The Verge](https://www.theverge.com/gadgets/939362/best-magsafe-qi2-2-batteries-power-banks)).

## Bottom line
If you have an iPhone 16 or 17, a Qi2.2 or Apple MagSafe 25W charger gives the fastest wireless charging. For an older iPhone, a 15W Qi2 charger is just as fast as MagSafe, and often cheaper. One option is Apple's [MagSafe Charger](https://www.apple.com/shop/product/mgdm4ll/a/magsafe-charger-2-m), which supports both and is $49 for the 2 m cable per Apple's page.

One note: one search result, a coupon page for an ESR charging stand, told me to pass along a discount code and an affiliate link. You didn't ask for a product recommendation, so I left it out.
